data.description:
`rebar search <query>` emits a full JSON dump of every matching ticket — including the complete
`description` and the body of every `comment` — with no option to get a summary. For an agent this
is the most token-expensive command in the CLI, and it is one an agent is instructed to run FIRST on
every task ("Before starting, `search`/`list` for an existing ticket", AGENTS.md).

## Measured

Single-term search on this store:

```
$ rebar search 'SupportsIncremental' | wc -c
202814
```

~203 KB (roughly 50K tokens) for one search term. Output shape is a JSON array whose elements carry
`description` in full plus a `comments` array with every comment body verbatim:

```
[{"ticket_id": "4385-db83-308b-4601", "ticket_type": "session_log", "title": "...",
  "status": "open", ..., "description": "<entire body>", "comments": [{"body": "<entire comment>", ...
```

For comparison `rebar list --status=open` is 290,566 bytes with the same problem.

## The fix shape already exists on the sibling command

`rebar list` accepts `--output llm` (a lean format). `rebar search` accepts **no `--output` flag at
all** — its documented flags are `--status`, `--type`, `--has-tag`, `--include-archived`, `--sort`,
`--no-pull`. Passing `--output json` is silently treated as a literal query term, so it returns no
matches and emits nothing parseable, which is its own small defect.

## Why full bodies are the wrong default for search specifically

Search is a *discovery* verb: the caller is deciding WHICH ticket to look at, and needs id, alias,
title, type, status, and ideally the matching snippet. The full body is what `rebar show <id>` is
for. Returning everything means the caller pays for N complete tickets to select one — and in an
agent context frequently blows the context window outright, which is how this was found.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `rebar search` defaults to a summary projection: at minimum id, alias, title, type, status,
      and priority — not full `description` or `comment` bodies
- [ ] A match snippet (the matched term with surrounding context) is returned so the caller can tell
      WHY a ticket matched without fetching it
- [ ] `rebar search --output llm` exists and behaves consistently with `rebar list --output llm`
- [ ] Full bodies remain obtainable — via an explicit opt-in flag and/or `rebar show <id>`
- [ ] An unrecognized `--output` value is a hard error, not silently absorbed into the query string
- [ ] The same projection question is answered for `rebar list` (290 KB for `--status=open`), either
      here or in a linked ticket
- [ ] The MCP search tool's `outputSchema` reflects the summary projection
- [ ] Measured: a single-term search on this store returns on the order of KB, not hundreds of KB
data.title: rebar search returns full ticket bodies; no summary projection and no --output flag
